project: Infinite You — Factory Definitions Packaging and Snapshot Consolidation
description: Publish focused Factory Definitions packaging and snapshot capabilities, preserve package and snapshot source/artifact fidelity, validate integrity before mutation, produce deterministic snapshot identity, return typed missing/malformed/integrity outcomes, and migrate System Initialization to the narrow packaging capability without changing runtime, session, event, recording, target, transport, generated API, or frontend behavior.

context.customerAsk: Consolidate package installation/distribution and loaded or initial snapshot behavior behind explicit Factory Definitions operations. Publish narrow packaging and snapshot capabilities, migrate one coherent consumer, preserve artifact/source fidelity, validate packages before installation, produce deterministic snapshot identity, and return typed missing, malformed, and integrity-failure outcomes. Carry the implementation through behavioral verification, review, required CI, explicit feedback resolution, conflict reconciliation, and actual PR merge.
context.problem: Factory Definitions already owns packaged catalogs, installers, snapshot capture, import preparation, materialization, and their effects, but callers encounter them through a broad root, standalone function operations, or aggregate callback structs. The fragmented surface does not itself guarantee validation before writes, package and artifact round-trip fidelity, deterministic snapshot identity, or distinguishable typed failures, and it creates pressure to absorb definition artifacts into runtime or session ownership.
context.solution: Expose separate narrow, injectable Factory Definitions capabilities for packaged catalog resolution/installation and loaded or explicit snapshot capture/import/materialization. Keep effects behind directly injected Factory Definitions ports, use detached values and typed errors, verify complete content before atomic commit, construct capabilities once in canonical wire, and migrate System Initialization to the focused packaging capability while retaining out-of-scope compatibility forwarding.

acceptanceCriteria: Factory Definitions publishes separate focused packaging and snapshot capabilities whose request/result and error contracts do not expose private implementations, raw collaborator callbacks, Factory Runtime, Factory Sessions, Events, or Recordings types.

A valid published package can be resolved, installed, and loaded back with its selected representation, canonical Factory meaning, authored-source information, and bundled artifact bytes preserved; package validation and integrity checks complete before target mutation.

Equivalent loaded or explicit definitions produce the same deterministic snapshot identity, meaningful definition or artifact changes produce a different identity, and snapshot import/materialization preserves source and artifact content.

Missing, malformed, unsupported, and integrity-failing package or snapshot inputs return stable typed classifications with sensitive-safe context and do not expose partial success or leave a newly changed target.

System Initialization consumes only the focused packaging capability and retains existing built-in installation ordering, create/skip/replace results, repeat-run behavior, and failure propagation; focused capability construction is inert and directly injected.
No generated API, Factory Runtime opening, Factory Session state ownership, target derivation, Factory Event, Recordings, CLI/HTTP/MCP behavior, or frontend behavior changes.
Quality gates pass: Typecheck, formatting, lint, package-boundary checks, focused tests, and applicable repository test suites are terminal and passing.

Delivery continues through implementation and correctness-first review until required CI is terminal and passing, every blocking PR conversation is explicitly addressed, shared-file or baseline conflicts and merge conflicts are resolved, and the PR is actually merged; opened, green, approved, or ready-to-merge is not complete.

userStories.title: Install validated packages with source and artifact fidelity
userStories.description: As an operator installing a built-in Factory, I want Factory Definitions to validate and install the selected package as one owned operation so that invalid content cannot mutate my definitions and valid source and artifacts remain faithful.
acceptanceCriteria: The focused packaging capability lists and resolves published package identities and installs a selected supported format without requiring the caller to pass package bytes, catalog callbacks, installer callbacks, or filesystem effects.

Installing a valid package and loading the installed Factory back yields the same canonical Factory meaning, public identity, selected JSON/YAML/YML representation, authored-source information, and byte-equivalent bundled artifacts as the published package.
Package identity, selected format, definition structure, bundled-file paths, and declared content integrity are checked before any target directory is created, replaced, or otherwise mutated.

A missing package identity, malformed definition, unsupported or unavailable representation, and package/artifact integrity mismatch each return a stable Factory Definitions typed classification that callers can inspect with standard Go error matching.
Every validation or integrity failure leaves a previously installed target byte-for-byte unchanged and leaves an absent target absent; no successful result or partial installation facts are returned.
Existing create, skip, and replace outcomes remain deterministic, including preservation of the requested authored root filename for JSON, YAML, and YML installs.

Focused behavioral tests cover successful package round trips for supported representations, bundled artifact preservation, validation-before-write, missing and malformed packages, unsupported formats, integrity failures, and unchanged targets after failure.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented the direct Packaging capability with detached catalog values, pre-mutation representation/artifact integrity validation, typed package-input failures, selected JSON/YAML/YML root fidelity, and focused behavioral coverage. Verified with Factory Definitions/catalog/wire/CLI tests, generated-catalog and wire reproducibility checks, typecheck, and make test. The repository-wide package-boundary gate remains red on 141 pre-existing violations outside this story.

userStories.title: Capture and materialize deterministic definition snapshots
userStories.description: As a maintainer of definition portability, I want Factory Definitions to own deterministic loaded-definition snapshots so that equivalent definitions can be identified reliably and restored without losing source or artifacts.
acceptanceCriteria: The focused snapshot capability captures loaded and explicit Factory definitions, prepares raw snapshot payloads for import, and materializes detached snapshots without requiring callers to provide representation mappers, codecs, portable-file callbacks, Runtime handles, Session state, or Recordings collaborators.

Repeated capture of logically equivalent definition, runtime-definition, metadata, source, and bundled-artifact content yields the same non-empty snapshot identity regardless of map iteration or input object allocation; a meaningful definition, runtime binding, source, metadata, or artifact-content change yields a different identity.

Capture followed by serialization, import preparation, and materialization preserves canonical Factory meaning, source directory/authored-source facts, runtime worker/workstation definitions, metadata, relative artifact paths, and artifact bytes.

Missing snapshot input or required source/artifact content, malformed snapshot payload, unsafe materialization path, and declared identity or artifact integrity mismatch each return a stable Factory Definitions typed classification.
Snapshot validation and integrity checks finish before materialization mutates the target; failure returns no partial success facts and leaves an existing target unchanged or an absent target absent.
Snapshot results and nested metadata/artifact values are detached from caller-owned and implementation-owned mutable state.

Focused behavioral tests cover deterministic identity, identity changes for meaningful content changes, snapshot round trips, detached results, missing and malformed inputs, unsafe paths, integrity failures, and no mutation on failure.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Published the focused Factory Definitions Snapshots capability with deterministic SHA-256 identities, detached loaded/explicit capture, typed input failures, artifact integrity verification, and staged atomic materialization. Behavioral coverage proves source/runtime/metadata/artifact round trips, stable identities, detachment, and pre-mutation failure safety. Verified Factory Definitions and wire tests, repeated race coverage, vet, typecheck, and diff validation; repository-wide package-boundary and package-file-count gates retain their existing shared baselines.

userStories.title: Bootstrap packaged Factories through the focused capability
userStories.description: As an operator initializing the system, I want built-in Factories installed through the focused Factory Definitions packaging capability so that bootstrap behavior stays stable without depending on broader definition services or callback bundles.
acceptanceCriteria: System Initialization receives one focused Factory Definitions packaging capability through canonical construction and no longer receives separate package catalog and installer callback aggregates for its built-in installation workflow.

For the same published catalog and filesystem state, initialization processes built-in packages in the same deterministic order and reports the same create, skip, and replace outcomes and installed locations as before.

Repeated initialization remains idempotent, and a typed missing, malformed, unsupported, or integrity-failing package outcome stops or reports initialization according to the existing failure policy without masking its Factory Definitions classification.

Construction injects the same capability instance directly, performs no catalog lookup, package validation, filesystem read/write, lifecycle activation, or cache population, and introduces no service locator, dependency bag, secondary injector, or runtime-time construction path.

Focused System Initialization and canonical-wire behavioral tests prove successful and repeated bootstrap, typed failure propagation, narrow dependency use, and inert construction; they do not assert method inventories or source-file topology.
Factory Runtime opening, initial-snapshot timing, Factory Session current-state ownership, target derivation, Events, Recordings, transports, and generated APIs remain behaviorally unchanged.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
